properties.statement:
AN INSTANCE OF THE RISK BL-185 RECORDS, WITH A MEASURED COST — and it is the agent's own working order, not somebody else's.

BL-185 has carried Anthony's words since 2026-08-03: "Developing tests as you design is extremely important. It shapes system architecture, forces clear thinking about edge cases early... Confirmation bias: Testing code you already wrote proves what it does, not necessarily what it should do." He raised the same question again on 2026-08-11 — the TENTH time in one session that a fresh thought landed on something the graph already held, and the only one where the prior record is his own verbatim reasoning on an OPEN fork nobody has chosen.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY DONE, TWICE, ON 2026-08-11:
  PR #149 (spawn_daemon)      implementation first, then tests, then mutation-checking
  PR #151 (search-first)      implementation first, then tests, then mutation-checking
Neither was test-first. Both were mutation-checked, which is this repo's real rigour and is a DIFFERENT property: mutation-checking proves a test can fail, it does not prove the test asks the right question.

⭐ THE COST WAS MEASURABLE AND IS THE POINT. PR #151's check refused two requirements whose statements were three words long ("Session A wrote this." / "Session B wrote this.") — a plainly wrong result, found by CI on an unrelated suite, not by any test written for the feature. The cause was an absent signal rather than a bad threshold: near-empty documents share most of their tokens by construction. THAT IS A BOUNDARY CONDITION, and "what are the boundary values" is precisely the question test-first forces before an author is attached to an implementation. It is also the GENESIS case — a young design is all short statements — so the miss was not exotic.

ANTHONY'S CRITERIA, 2026-08-11, recorded because BL-185 does not carry them and the fork should be judged against something: a good test is VALID (measures what it claims, not a side effect), ISOLATED (no dependence on other tests or shared state), REPEATABLE (same result every run under identical conditions), FOCUSED (one behaviour, not several), and FAST. It should target the HAPPY PATH, EDGE CASES (boundaries, extremes, unusual inputs), ERROR CONDITIONS (failures, missing data, bad input, stress), and THE CONTRACT RATHER THAN THE IMPLEMENTATION, so an internal change does not produce a false failure.

📌 SCORING PR #151's OWN SUITE AGAINST THEM, honestly, because a fact that only indicts the past is not evidence:
  valid        yes — asserts the refusal, the rollback and the created node, not side effects
  isolated     yes — each case builds its own in-memory service
  repeatable   yes in practice, but SENSITIVE TO CORPUS CONTENT: the threshold is relative to
               other nodes present, so a case is only as stable as its seeding. One test sat on
               the boundary during development and had to be re-seeded.
  focused      mostly; the revision case must seed a neighbour or it proves nothing
  fast         yes, sub-second
  happy path   covered
  edge cases   COVERED ONLY AFTER CI FOUND ONE. Not designed in.
  error cond.  NOT COVERED. The `unavailable` branch — the search itself failing — has ZERO
               tests. It is the branch that exists to satisfy req:no-silent-fallback, and
               nothing proves it fires.
  contract     mixed. Two assertions match literal words in the refusal text ("SHARPEN",
               "distinct_from"); the contract is that BOTH routes are named, and the test reads
               the wording rather than the property.

SO THE HONEST SCORE IS SIX AND A HALF OF NINE, with the two misses landing exactly where implement-first predicts they would: edge cases and error conditions.

⚠️ WHAT THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR. It is one agent, one day, two PRs, and both shipped working and gated. It says nothing about whether test-first would have been FASTER, and BL-185's own guard rail stands: Anthony's caveat that this "may not apply to or be feasible for all project types", and the adopt path where every recovered test is necessarily after the fact. A reading that scored implement-first as failure would repeat BL-179's punish-correct-work trap.

📌 A SEPARATE FINDING FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS: MUTATION-CHECKING IS THIS PROJECT'S STRONGEST TEST DISCIPLINE AND IS WRITTEN DOWN NOWHERE AS A RULE. At least eight Verifications record it in their own text (evidence-quality, ility, no-fabricated-repairs, siblings-are-not-merged-away, edges-need-both-ends, supporting-is-not-conflict, the-server-says-when-it-is-stale, search-first-forces-a-choice) and AGENTS.md does not mention it. It is a convention held by imitation — every agent that does it learned it by reading a test file. That is the same shape as the search-first rule living in five skills and firing only when one is loaded.
